species.real: The cold, acid, airless water of a raised bog tans skin like leather but slowly dissolves bone, which is why some bog bodies come out of the peat oddly flattened.
species.name: Peatling

dex.text: Rises out of the cut peat at dusk, brown as strong tea and twice as stewed. Wants to tell you about the Iron Age. At length.
dex.fact: Lindow Man was found by peat cutters at Lindow Moss, near Wilmslow in Cheshire, in 1984. The acid, airless bog had kept his skin, hair and beard for about 2,000 years.

species.real: Lindow Man was hit on the head, strangled and had his throat cut, all around the first century AD, which has led to a lot of talk about ritual sacrifice and very little agreement.
species.name: Lindwight

dex.text: An old soul of the moss, leathery and calm, with the patience of something that has already waited two thousand years. Hates being dug up. Fair enough.
dex.fact: The newspapers nicknamed Lindow Man 'Pete Marsh'. His body is now in the British Museum, and his stomach held the remains of a last meal of charred bread.
